speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have had a fever and changes in your mental state for the last two days; can you tell me exactly what those mental changes look like and if you have experienced any seizures?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) secondary to haloperidol use. Given the history of tics and current haloperidol use, combined with fever and altered mental status, I am highly concerned about NMS. Please confirm if you are experiencing muscle rigidity or tremors, and check your vital signs immediately for tachycardia and hypertension.
